title: should have / shouldn't have: looking back
tagline: Use should have + past participle to say what was the right (or wrong) thing to do in the past.
why: At B1 you need to talk about mistakes and regrets: I should have studied more, you shouldn't have shouted. B1 Preliminary tests modal verbs in the multiple-choice cloze, and in the Writing email you often say what you wish you had done differently. Getting the form right also makes your speaking sound natural, especially with the short sound should've.

hook.text: Mateo: "I failed the quiz. I should have studied more!" Sofia: "Yes, and you shouldn't have played games all night." Mateo: "I know. I should have listened to you!"
hook.ask: Mateo is talking about last night, not tonight. What three words come before studied, played and listened? Do you see the same pattern each time?

diagrams.title: Looking back from now
diagrams.caption: We look back at the past and say what would have been better: should have + past participle.

diagrams.title: Build the sentence
diagrams.caption: After should have the main verb is always the past participle: studied, shouted, called, gone, seen.

rows.label: Idea
cells: regret or criticism about what happened

head: Form
Pattern
Example
rows: What / Why should + subject + have + participle?

use.point: Regret about something you did or didn't do

examples.text: I should have taken an umbrella. I'm wet!
examples.note: I didn't take one, and now I regret it

examples.text: Nadia should have gone to bed earlier.
examples.note: she stayed up, and now she is tired

examples.text: We should have left home at seven.
examples.note: we were late, so it was the better plan

examples.text: You shouldn't have shouted at your sister.
examples.note: you shouted, and it was wrong
he told it, and that was a mistake

examples.text: They shouldn't have left the door open.
examples.note: they left it open, and now the cat has escaped

use.point: Advice about now or later, or about the past?

examples.text: You should study more for the next test.
examples.note: advice for the future: should + base verb

examples.text: You should have studied more for the last test.

use.point: Questions and the short spoken form

examples.note: very informal speech, not for writing

watch_out.why: It sounds like of, but it is have. Say and write should've or should have.
After should have use the past participle (gone), not the past simple (went).
For the past you need have + participle. should + past form is wrong.

watch_out.wrong: She should have to call me.

watch_out.why: After a modal verb, have never changes: have, not has.

watch_out.wrong: Should I have to study more yesterday?
watch_out.why: In a question, should comes first, then the subject, then have + participle.

l1.why: Spanish haber + participio becomes should have + past participle, so the verb needs its participle form.
The negative goes with should: shouldn't have, never didn't should.
You had to go means it was necessary and you went. Should have gone means you didn't go but it was better.

l1.wrong: I should of stayed at home.
l1.why: Debí/debería haber is always should have, never should of.

remember.tip: Think of it as a time machine: should have + past participle sends your advice back to yesterday. Say should've to practise the sound.

dialogue.title: After the match
dialogue.context: Mateo's team lost the match and Liam, Nadia and Sofia talk to him and Miss Vega on the bench.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I can't believe we lost. I should have passed the ball to Liam!

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: True, and I should have shouted louder. I was free!

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: We shouldn't have stopped to argue about it during the game.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: And we should have warmed up properly. I was cold in the first half.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Should we have changed the plan at half-time? I think so.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: You should have kept the ball more and you shouldn't have kicked it so far.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Next time I shouldn't have... I mean, I shouldn't shout at the referee!

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Liam, you shouldn't have said that to him today. It was rude!

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Easy to say now. But we should have thought about it earlier.

items.sentence: Mateo failed the test. He ___ harder.
You didn't tell me the truth. You ___ me.
items.why: regret about the past: should have + participle

items.sentence: It's cold outside. You ___ your coat now.
items.why: advice for now = should + base verb

items.sentence: Nadia ate five cakes and feels sick. She ___ so many.
items.why: she did it, and it was a mistake

items.sentence: We missed the bus. We ___ earlier.
items.why: the better past action: should have left

items.sentence: Liam shouted at his sister. He ___ that.
It was a secret! You ___ anyone.

practice.instructions: Complete with should have or shouldn't have and the verb in brackets, in the correct form.

items.sentence: I forgot my homework. I ___ (pack) my bag last night.
He was only joking. You ___ (shout) at him.
She has a headache. She ___ (sleep) more.
The fish was old and he felt ill. He ___ (eat) it.
Miss Vega gave me good advice. I ___ (listen) to her.
Now the cat has escaped! They ___ (leave) the door open.
The task was hard. Mateo ___ (ask) for help earlier.

practice.instructions: Put the words in order. Tap them one by one.

items.answer: He shouldn't have eaten all the cake.
Should we have waited for Liam?
I should have studied more last night.
They shouldn't have laughed at her.

practice.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first, using the word given. Use no more than three words.

items.first: I didn't study, and that was a mistake.
It was wrong of you to take my pen.
Why didn't you ask me for help?
It's a pity Nadia didn't come to the party.
Liam was wrong to tell the secret.
I think it was a mistake to wait so long.

can_do: I can say what was the right thing to do in the past with should have + past participle.
I can criticise a past action with shouldn't have, and tell it apart from should + base verb for now.
I can ask Should we have…? and say should've in a natural way.
summary: Use should have + past participle for a regret or for what would have been better in the past.
Use shouldn't have + past participle when a past action was a mistake.
should + base verb is advice for now or later; should have is for the past.
In speech we say should've, but we never write should of.
